children.text: Opened in 1991, Shangri-La Plaza is a flagship mall of Ortigas Center, directly linked to MRT-3 Shaw Boulevard Station. Its open-air-style dining hub Streetscape, the Red Carpet cinema and the annual Christmas tree lighting are the main draws.
Shangri-La Plaza is a large shopping mall at the corner of EDSA and Shaw Boulevard in Mandaluyong, Metro Manila. It opened on
November 21
, 1991, and is run by the Kuok Group, the owner of the Shangri-La hotel chain. It is described as having more than 300 shops and restaurants, and it has long stood as a landmark of Ortigas Center.

The building is divided into the Main Wing, the East Wing added in 2013, and the North Wing, which doubles as a parking building. The atrium on the 2nd floor of the Main Wing serves as a stage for big events, and Edsa Shangri-La hotel, the One Shangri-La Place residential towers and MRT-3 Shaw Boulevard Station all connect directly to the mall, so you can get around without stepping outside even in the rain. Floor by floor, the Main Wing has one basement level and six retail floors. The basement holds the Food Forum, The Marketplace supermarket and electronics shops; on the 5th floor, The Fifth is aimed at younger shoppers and sits beside a health and wellness zone; and the 6th floor has The Ledge, a cluster of restaurants, plus the cinema and the chapel. The North Wing is a multi-level parking building with a small strip of banks, a drugstore, snack shops, bars, restaurants and a salon facing EDSA.

What makes it handy for travelers is that you can finish many errands in one place. Designer and international brand shopping, a movie, a meal at popular Filipino restaurants and a supermarket run are all possible in one air-conditioned building, which makes it a good place to rest from midday heat or a sudden downpour. Manila is a city with heavy traffic, so the mall's location is a big advantage. Get off the MRT-3 at Shaw Boulevard Station and you are already inside the mall, with the hotel and residential towers continuing above it. You can plan one day around the historic sites of downtown Manila and another day of shopping and dining here to pace your energy.

From mid-November to late December in particular, the tree lighting in the Grand Atrium, the large tree, weekend choir performances and the year-end fireworks make it one of the first places in Manila to feel the Christmas mood. This article is based on publicly available sources; store lineups and event schedules change often, so check the mall's official channels before you visit.

blocks.title: Main Wing atrium and Grand Atrium

children.text: The atrium in the center of the Main Wing's 2nd floor is the mall's main stage. Seasonal events, exhibits and performances take place here, and because the escalators skip the odd-numbered floors and go straight to the 2nd, 4th and 6th floors, the layout is easy to take in at a glance.
In 2025 the lighting ceremony took place in the Grand Atrium on
November 15
, with a large tree suspended from the ceiling as the centerpiece. Choir and dance performances followed on December weekends, and the season closed with fireworks on
December 30
. The schedule differs every year, so check this year's announcements. The lighting event also featured choirs such as the Philippine Madrigal Singers and a ballet performance.

Streetscape, which opened anew in early April 2025, is an open-air-feeling dining space reported to cover about 3,000 sq m on the ground floor near the main wing entrance. Popular restaurants such as Wildflour, A Mano and The Wholesome Table are located here.

The former Shang Cineplex was relaunched under a new concept in late 2018 and sits on the 6th and 7th floors. It has five theaters, and the Premiere theater has 70 leatherette recliners with an adjoining bar and lounge. Tickets can also be booked online. Besides new releases, Metro Manila Film Festival entries have been shown here from
December 25
in the holiday season.

The Ledge on the 6th floor gathers restaurant chains such as Harlan + Holden, Manam, Red Lotus and Gingerlily. The range runs from Filipino to Chinese and Japanese cooking, which makes it an easy choice for a family meal.

blocks.title: Upscale brands in the East Wing

children.text: The East Wing, which opened in 2013, focuses on upscale and international brands and restaurants and connects to the Main Wing by bridgeways. It also serves as the podium of the two One Shangri-La Place towers.

blocks.title: Rustan's department store and basement grocery shopping

children.text: Rustan's in the Main Wing is a high-end department store spread over four floors. The basement has the Food Forum, The Marketplace supermarket and electronics shops, which makes it convenient for local groceries and snack souvenirs.

The 6th floor has the St. Padre Pio Chapel, a Catholic chapel. You can reach it by escalator from the 5th floor or through a hallway from the Main Wing, and shoppers stop in to pray quietly or attend Mass. It is a small place where you can get a close look at Filipino Catholic culture.
Arrive around opening time and look around the Main Wing atrium and the 2nd floor. Weekday mornings are relatively quiet.
Browse snacks and groceries for souvenirs at The Marketplace and the Food Forum in the basement.
Have lunch at Streetscape or The Ledge. Popular restaurants have waits on weekends, so it is better to go early.
Walk through the East Wing and Rustan's to shop, then rest at a cafe.
Watch a movie at Red Carpet on the 6th floor, or take a brief look at St. Padre Pio Chapel.
Last screening times and store hours can differ from day to day, so check the notices on site.

items.title: Christmas evening course
items.subtitle: An outing in the lighting season

children.text: Enter the mall directly from MRT-3 Shaw Boulevard Station.
See the large tree and decorations in the Grand Atrium and take photos. The evening hours are crowded.
Have dinner at the open-air-style dining area.
On days with a season-closing event, check for performances or fireworks at Streetscape before heading home.

items.title: From Manila's airport by taxi or Grab

children.text: The travel time from Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) to the mall varies greatly with road conditions, so confirm locally. It is best to avoid rush hours.
When using an airport taxi or Grab, tell the driver your destination as Shangri-La Plaza or the entrance of Edsa Shangri-La hotel.
MRT-3 Shaw Boulevard Station (YL07) connects directly to the mall.
From Ayala Station in Makati or Cubao Station in Quezon City, many sections can be traveled without transferring. Check operating hours and fares locally.
Buses run along EDSA, and jeepneys serve routes toward Shaw Boulevard.
The area is heavily congested, so the MRT or Grab is easier for first-time visitors.
The mall has multi-level parking, with entrances from both EDSA and Shaw Boulevard. Valet service is reported to be available, but confirm the rates locally.
As an indoor mall it can be visited year-round. From mid-November to late December, however, the Christmas events are at their richest, and weekend evenings are very crowded as a result.
It is a good air-conditioned refuge in the hot March–May season and during rainy-season showers. For quiet shopping, weekday mornings are recommended.

During the Christmas season, the lighting-ceremony day and days with weekend choir performances are the busiest. If you want to take photos at a leisurely pace, aim for a weekday evening or just after opening, and for timed events such as the year-end fireworks, secure a spot an hour before they start. Business hours may change just before and after New Year.

Edsa Shangri-La, Manila hotel and The St. Francis Shangri-La Place are right next to the mall, so for a shopping-focused trip, basing yourself nearby is an option. Room rates vary greatly by season, so check on booking sites.

Streetscape and The Ledge have the most dining choices. Places such as Wildflour, Manam, Harlan + Holden and Starbucks Reserve are listed, and the basement Food Forum is handy for a quick meal. Korean food is easier to find outside the mall, around Ortigas.

For family trips, a children's play area and light activity programs are reported, making it a good place to rest with kids. Individual stores often move or change, so confirm that a restaurant you want to visit is still open using the mall directory or official channels.

After finishing your shopping and before returning to your hotel, it is convenient to pick up water, fruit and light snacks at The Marketplace in the basement. If you need a late-night meal, look into hotel room service or restaurants outside the mall.
Some entrances link directly to the MRT-3 station, so you can get in comfortably even on rainy days.
It is quiet on weekday mornings, and weekend lunch and dinner bring long waits at restaurants.
Check the Christmas-season lighting schedule and performance times in the mall's official announcements in advance.
The cinema is on the 6th and 7th floors, so follow the floor directory. Elevators are nearby.
The air conditioning inside is strong, so bring a light jacket.
Combining the mall with nearby SM Megamall and Ortigas Center makes for a full day.
Cards are widely accepted, but carry some small cash too.
Amenities such as lounges, baby-changing stations, free Wi-Fi and accessible restrooms are reported.
Receipts can sometimes be used for parking discounts or movie points, so do not throw them away; check the mall's notices.
Around the mall, the EDSA stretch and parking lots are extremely congested at year-end and on weekends, so the MRT or Grab is recommended.
To guard against pickpockets, carry your bag in front of you on crowded escalators and MRT platforms.
Opening hours are generally listed as 10:00–21:00, but they differ by store and on holidays, so confirm.
Check that taxis use the meter, and use a ride-hailing app if possible.
Christmas-season events and the store lineup change every year.
Crossing EDSA on foot is dangerous; always use the overpasses and the mall's connecting walkways.
The business and commercial district the mall belongs to, with tall buildings and malls packed together, so places connect with short trips. It pairs well in a one-day plan.
Another large mall close by along EDSA, with a wide choice of cinemas, restaurants and brand stores.
A shopping destination in the Shaw Boulevard direction, good for shopping and eating. Go by car or Grab.
A city bordering the east of the mall, with Ortigas-area offices, government facilities and restaurants, good to explore together. Travel time depends on traffic.
Visitor guides mention the Lopez Museum as a cultural venue within walking distance of the mall. Check its opening hours in advance.
